title: Business Analyst II
description: Are you a strategic planner and problem-solver? Are you looking to develop your Data Analyst career? About The Team Mercury is RX’s global registration and eCommerce platform, supporting the journeys that bring visitors and exhibitors into our events. Its capabilities span registration, purchasing, badging and onsite access, connecting customer experiences with the data and business systems behind them. We work across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Product Success and regional business teams to deliver reliable services, improve customer experiences and create measurable business value. About The Role We’re seeking a Business Analyst with a strong focus on User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to bridge product delivery and business validation. You’ll coordinate testing, help business users evaluate new features, manage feedback, and communicate releases in clear, accessible language. The focus is hands-on business acceptance and coordination—not software development or test automation engineering. Responsibilities (What You’ll Do) Plan and coordinate business acceptance testing Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and Business Analysts to understand desired outcomes, user journeys, business rules, and acceptance criteria. Turn requirements into practical, risk-based UAT scenarios covering standard journeys, exceptions, and relevant regional variations. Coordinate testing scope and schedules, providing participants with clear instructions, test-event links, and prerequisites. Work with engineering, QA, and configuration teams to ensure environments, test data, and configurations are ready before testing. Perform hands-on business validation and help users investigate and reproduce unexpected results. Manage feedback, defects, and acceptance evidence Maintain a consolidated record of business feedback and communicate test completion, outstanding observations, and potential enhancements. Separate defects from configuration issues, clarification requests, and enhancement ideas, working with product and technical teams to agree next steps. Document reproducible issues, including expected and actual results, supporting evidence, and business impact, and coordinate retesting after fixes. Report progress, coverage, blockers, and residual risks so decision-makers can clearly assess readiness. Coordinate acceptance evidence and follow-up while keeping approval and validation accountability with the relevant Business Units. Support release communication and continuous improvement Prepare business-facing release updates that explain what changed, why it matters, and any relevant limitations or actions. Keep testing guidance, feedback records, and supporting documentation accessible to global stakeholders. Create reusable scenarios and checklists to improve consistency and reduce repeated effort across releases. Apply lessons from UAT and production issues to strengthen future acceptance coverage and identify gaps earlier. Collaborate across regions and time zones, keeping dependencies, decisions, and ownership clear. Requirements (What You’ll Bring) Practical experience in UAT, business analysis, functional testing, or a similar role supporting user-facing digital products. Experience translating requirements and business processes into clear acceptance criteria and end-to-end test scenarios. Ability to organize testing with business users, balance competing priorities, and follow issues through to documented outcomes. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to explain business impact as well as technical symptoms. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing user guidance, test summaries, and release updates. Experience with issue-tracking and collaborative documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence, or equivalents. Understanding of Agile delivery and the differences between engineering QA, business acceptance, and release approval. A collaborative approach and confidence working with technical and non-technical stakeholders in a distributed team. Useful, But Not Essential, Skills Experience with event registration, ticketing, eCommerce, or other transaction-based customer journeys. Familiarity with payments, invoicing, discounts, upgrades, entitlements, or integrations between customer-facing and back-office systems. Exposure to onsite operational tools, badge management, or access-control workflows. Awareness of accessibility, localization, and data-quality considerations in business acceptance testing. Experience with test-management tools, basic data queries, or API-testing tools to support investigations. What Success Looks Like Business users know what to test, how to participate, and where to provide feedback. Critical business journeys have clear acceptance coverage and traceable results. Defects and feedback are actionable, assigned, and followed through, with unresolved risks visible before release decisions. Business approvers receive concise evidence to support acceptance decisions. Release communications clearly explain changes and limitations, helping teams prepare for adoption. Reusable guidance and lessons learned make each testing cycle more effective. Why join us? Help shape digital experiences that connect online registration with the live event experience. You’ll work across product, technology, and business operations, building domain knowledge while improving how changes are validated and communicated. RX values collaboration, inclusion, curiosity, and learning, with opportunities to contribute across a global network. Work in a Way That Works for You We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous well-being initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals. Working for You Benefits We know that your wellbeing and happiness are key to a long and successful career. These are some of the benefits we are delighted to offer: Comprehensive Health Insurance: Covers you, your immediate family, and parents Enhanced Health Insurance Options: Competitive rates negotiated by the company Group Life Insurance: Ensuring financial security for your loved ones Group Accident Insurance: Extra protection for accidental death and permanent disablement Flexible Working Arrangement: Achieve a harmonious work-life balance Employee Assistance Program: Access support for personal and work-related challenges Medical Screening: Your well-being is a top priority Modern Family Benefits: Maternity, paternity, and adoption support Long-Service Awards: Recognizing dedication and commitment New Baby Gift: Celebrating the joy of parenthood Subsidized Meals in Chennai: Enjoy delicious meals at discounted rates Various Paid Time Off: Take time off with Casual Leave, Sick Leave, Privilege Leave, Compassionate Leave, Special Sick Leave, and Gazetted Public Holidays About The Business RX is a global leader in events and exhibitions, leveraging industry expertise, data, and technology to build businesses for individuals, communities, and organizations. RX empowers businesses to thrive by leveraging data-driven insights and digital solutions. title: Engineer II, System validation Test - Insight QA
description: About The Role We are looking for an Engineer II in System Validation Testing with 3 to 5 years of experience to join our cloud network management quality engineering team. The role focuses on hands-on testing of a cloud-hosted platform used to onboard, configure, monitor and manage networking devices such as access points, switches and routers. The engineer will work with senior QA engineers, developers and product teams to understand requirements, design and execute tests, automate repeatable workflows, investigate failures and contribute to reliable releases across the device, network, cloud, API and web or mobile application layers. Key Responsibilities Cloud Network Management Testing Understand feature requirements and expected customer workflows for cloud-managed access points, switches and routers. Test device onboarding, discovery, provisioning, configuration and removal workflows. Validate device-to-cloud communication, cloud-to-device operations and configuration synchronization. Test device status, statistics, alerts, notifications and basic remote-management workflows. Validate firmware upgrade, reconnect, recovery and factory-reset scenarios under guidance. Execute tests across common LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi and multi-device network setups. Test Planning and Execution Review user stories, acceptance criteria and functional specifications with the QA team. Create and maintain clear test scenarios and test cases covering positive, negative, boundary and recovery conditions. Prepare test data and configure required devices, accounts, subscriptions and environments. Execute functional, integration, system, regression, compatibility and end-to-end tests. Record results accurately, report coverage gaps and escalate blockers early. Retest resolved defects and run focused regression for impacted workflows. API Cloud and Data Validation Test REST APIs using tools such as Postman and automation libraries. Validate request and response data, status codes, authentication, authorization and error handling. Verify consistency across APIs, backend services, database records and user interfaces. Test asynchronous operations, events and notifications with support from senior engineers. Use AWS logs, dashboards and application telemetry to investigate test failures. Perform smoke and regression validation in QA and staging environments. Networking and Troubleshooting Apply networking fundamentals including TCP/IP, IPv4 and IPv6, DHCP, DNS, ARP, ICMP, HTTP and HTTPS, VLANs, routing, switching, NAT, LAN, WAN and Wi-Fi. a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright TypeScript pytest Python FastAPI PostgreSQL SQL REST OpenAPI GitHub Actions Docker HL7 v2 FHIR ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest.
